sections.title: Choosing Work and Setting a Direction

headwords.definition: the sequence of jobs and professional experiences a person has over time
examples: She hopes to build a career in public health.
Changing careers at forty gave him a stronger sense of purpose.

headwords.definition: a person's regular type of paid work
examples: Teaching is a demanding occupation, but it can be deeply rewarding.
The survey asked participants to state their occupation and highest qualification.

headwords.definition: a type of work that usually requires specialized education or training
examples: Nursing is a profession that combines technical knowledge with compassion.
She entered the legal profession after completing graduate school.

headwords.definition: work that a person feels especially suited to and strongly motivated to do
examples: He sees working with children as a vocation, not simply a way to earn money.
It took several jobs before Mina discovered her vocation in environmental education.

headwords.definition: the series of roles, choices, and stages through which a career develops
examples: Software testing was not her original career path, but she quickly enjoyed the work.
A mentor helped me see several career paths connected to my degree.

headwords.definition: the chances of finding good work and progressing in a particular field
examples: Students often consider career prospects when choosing a major.

headwords.definition: a strong feeling that a particular kind of work is personally meaningful
examples: For her, animal rescue became a calling after years of volunteering.

headwords.definition: something considered more important than other factors in a decision
examples: A predictable schedule is my main priority because I care for an elderly parent.

headwords.definition: giving a strong sense of purpose, satisfaction, or personal value
examples: I find tutoring fulfilling because I can see a student's confidence grow.

headwords.definition: right for a particular person, purpose, or situation
examples: A night shift would not be suitable for someone who has morning classes.

headwords.definition: a skill or quality that someone performs especially well
examples: Explaining difficult ideas in simple language is one of her main strengths.

headwords.definition: a natural ability or potential to learn a particular skill
examples: His aptitude for fixing machines led him toward technical training.

sections.title: Advancement, Career Change, and the Future of Work

headwords.definition: to move an employee to a more senior position

headwords.definition: to make progress toward a more senior or skilled position

headwords.definition: to formally leave a job by choice

headwords.definition: without paid work while available for and often seeking a job

headwords.definition: to learn new skills for a different job or changed occupation
